objectives: Survey biodiversity, deforestation, desertification, ozone, acid rain, plastics as global environmental issues.
Connect IPCC + Anthropocene framings to climate-vulnerable geographies.
Apply Brundtland, SDGs, planetary boundaries, ecological footprint, degrowth, and ecosystem-services frameworks.

slides.title: Environmental issues — hotspots, deforestation, desertification, ozone, plastics
slides.body:
**Environmental geography** studies humanity's transformation of the natural world + the spatial patterns of environmental change.

**Biodiversity hotspots — Norman Myers (1934-2019)**:
- *The Environmentalist* (1988); *Hotspots* (2000) with Conservation International. Defined a **biodiversity hotspot** as a region with **>1500 endemic vascular plant species** + **≥70% original habitat loss**.
- Originally 25 hotspots; now **36** covering ~2.4% of Earth's land surface yet harboring ~50% of plant + ~43% of vertebrate species.
- Examples: Mediterranean Basin, Cerrado, Atlantic Forest, California Floristic Province, Cape Floristic Region, Madagascar + Indian Ocean Islands, Sundaland, Wallacea, Tropical Andes, Mesoamerica, Mountains of Southwest China, Eastern Afromontane, Western Ghats + Sri Lanka, New Caledonia, Polynesia-Micronesia, Caribbean.
- Drives Conservation International + Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund (CEPF) priorities; concept criticized for under-weighting non-tropical + freshwater + marine biodiversity (countered by KBAs — Key Biodiversity Areas).

**Amazon deforestation (INPE PRODES + DETER)**:
- ~17% of Brazilian Amazon original forest lost; cumulative ~825000 km² cleared as of 2024.
- Drivers: cattle (~70% of clearance), soy expansion, illegal logging, mining, infrastructure (BR-319, BR-163).
- INPE PRODES (annual deforestation) + DETER (near-real-time alerts via MODIS + Landsat + Sentinel + CBERS) operationalize monitoring; Brazil's 2004-2012 reduction (~80% peak-to-trough) was a remote-sensing-enabled policy success; subsequent reversal (2019-2022) + recovery 2023-.
- **Tipping-point risk**: Carlos Nobre + Tom Lovejoy (2018) warned that ~20-25% deforestation + warming could trigger Amazon dieback into savanna over decades.

**Desertification + UNCCD**:
- **United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD, 1994)** — one of the three Rio Conventions (alongside UNFCCC + CBD).
- Drylands cover ~41% of Earth's land surface + support ~2 B people; ~10-20% are degrading.
- Hotspots: Sahel, Mongolia + N China, Central Asia, NE Brazil, Mediterranean, Australian rangelands, US Southwest, Horn of Africa.
- **Great Green Wall** (African Union, 2007-) — 8000 km tree + agroforestry belt across Sahel; partial success in Senegal + Ethiopia; broader challenges of land tenure + governance.

**Acid rain (1970s-1990s success)**:
- SO₂ + NOₓ from coal + industry → H₂SO₄ + HNO₃ in precipitation → forest + lake acidification.
- Major impacts: Scandinavian + Canadian + NE US forests + lakes; Black Forest + Eastern Europe; spruce die-off; freshwater fish loss.
- US 1990 Clean Air Act Amendments (cap-and-trade for SO₂); EU LCPD + Gothenburg Protocol; ~90% SO₂ reductions in US + Europe by 2010s.
- A geography of environmental success: source regions reduced emissions, downwind ecosystems recovered (with ongoing N + soil legacy issues). Now reappearing in regions of growing coal use (India, parts of China before SO₂ scrubbing).

**Ozone hole + Montreal Protocol 1987**:
- **Molina + Rowland (1974)** identified CFCs as stratospheric ozone destroyers; Nobel 1995 (with Crutzen).
- **Joe Farman + British Antarctic Survey (1985)** — discovered the **Antarctic ozone hole** in *Nature*.
- **Montreal Protocol (1987)** — single most successful international environmental treaty; phased out CFCs + HCFCs.
- Ozone hole peaked ~2000-2006; now slowly healing; expected recovery 2060-2080.
- **Kigali Amendment (2016)** — phase down HFCs (potent GHGs); side-benefit ~0.5°C avoided warming.

**Plastics + ocean gyres**:
- ~400 Mt plastic produced annually; ~10 Mt enters ocean.
- **Five major ocean gyres** accumulate floating plastic — North Pacific (Great Pacific Garbage Patch, ~1.6 M km²), South Pacific, North Atlantic, South Atlantic, Indian Ocean.
- Microplastics throughout marine food webs + soils + freshwater + drinking water + human tissue.
- **UN Plastics Treaty negotiations (INC-1 to INC-5, 2022-2024+)** — toward a global plastics agreement; stalled at INC-5 Busan 2024 over production caps.

slides.title: Climate change geography + the Anthropocene
slides.body:
**IPCC AR6 (2021-2023)** synthesis: human-induced warming ~1.1-1.3°C since 1850-1900; ~2.5-3°C projected by 2100 on current trajectory; ~1.5-2°C achievable with deep + rapid mitigation.

**Sea-level rise (SLR)**:
- Global mean SLR ~3.7 mm/yr (2006-2018), accelerating.
- Components: thermal expansion ~1.0 mm/yr; Greenland Ice Sheet ~0.8 mm/yr (acceleration); Antarctic Ice Sheet ~0.4 mm/yr (could accelerate dramatically from Thwaites + West Antarctic instability); glaciers ~0.6 mm/yr; land water storage ~0.4 mm/yr.
- IPCC AR6 likely SLR by 2100: 0.4-0.9 m (SSP1-2.6 to SSP5-8.5); high-end ~1.5-2 m cannot be ruled out due to ice-sheet uncertainty (DeConto + Pollard 2016; Pattyn + Morlighem 2020).
- Most-vulnerable geographies:
  - **Bangladesh** — 165 M on the Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna delta; ~1.2 m SLR + cyclone storm-surge intensification displaces ~13-15% of population.
  - **Tuvalu, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Maldives** — atoll nations facing existential threat. Tuvalu's 'digital nation' (2022) preserves sovereignty if territory disappears.
  - **Florida + Louisiana + Houston** — coastal subsidence + SLR + hurricanes.
  - **Vietnam Mekong Delta** — ~20 M; salinization + subsidence.
  - **Egypt Nile Delta** — ~40 M coastal residents; agriculture-water-energy nexus.
  - **Indonesia Jakarta** — sinking >25 cm/yr from groundwater extraction; Nusantara new capital project on Borneo.

**Cryosphere + Greenland + Antarctica**:
- **Greenland Ice Sheet** — 1.7 M km², ~7.4 m SLR equivalent if fully lost; surface mass balance increasingly negative since 1995; subglacial channels + meltwater feedback; tipping at ~1.5-3°C (Robinson + Calov + Ganopolski 2012).
- **Antarctic Ice Sheet** — East AIS stable so far; West AIS (Thwaites 'Doomsday Glacier', Pine Island) increasingly destabilizing — marine ice-sheet instability (Schoof 2007).
- **Sea ice** — Arctic summer minimum trending down ~13%/decade; possibly first ice-free September ~2030-2050; Antarctic sea ice unexpectedly collapsing since 2016.
- **Permafrost** — ~24% of NH land; ~1500 Pg C stored; thawing releases CO₂ + CH₄ + collapses infrastructure (Norilsk, NWT, Alaska); abrupt thaw (thermokarst, talik) under-modeled.
- **Mountain glaciers** — ~80% of Andean + Himalayan + European Alps glaciers projected to lose mass by 2100; water-supply consequences for downstream populations (Indus, Ganges-Brahmaputra, Yangtze, Mekong, Andean cities).

**Tropical-region warming + adaptation**:
- Tropical warming smaller in absolute °C but larger in **climate-velocity** terms — tropical species + crops have narrow thermal envelopes.
- Wet-bulb temperature thresholds (~35°C TW = human limit for outdoor labor); already exceeded in Persian Gulf + South Asia heatwaves.
- Coral reef bleaching — 2016 + 2017 + 2022 + 2024 mass-bleaching events; ~50% global coral lost since 1950.

**The Anthropocene**:
- **Paul Crutzen (1933-2021)** — Dutch atmospheric chemist; Nobel 1995 for ozone-CFC work; proposed (2000-2002) that human activity constitutes a new geological epoch. He coined **Anthropocene**.
- **Anthropocene Working Group (AWG, 2009-)** of the International Commission on Stratigraphy considered formalization; proposed **1952 plutonium fallout** + **Crawford Lake (Canada) GSSP**. **March 2024 SQS rejected formalization**; the term remains scientifically + culturally influential without formal stratigraphic status.
- **Stratigraphic markers**: anthropogenic radionuclides, microplastics, fly-ash, novel materials, novel species distributions, isotope shifts, soot, nitrogen-cycle alteration.
- **Great Acceleration (Steffen et al. 2015)** — post-1950 exponential rises in CO₂, GDP, population, urbanization, fertilizer, plastics, energy, dams, telecom, transport, biodiversity loss — define the Anthropocene's social-ecological signature.

**Critical perspectives**:
- **Capitalocene** (Jason Moore 2015) — capitalism as the driver, not 'humanity' generically.
- **Plantationocene** (Donna Haraway + Anna Tsing) — plantation logic as Anthropocene grammar.
- **Indigenous critique** — Anthropocene erases pre-1492 indigenous land + species management + collapses humanity into uniform agent.

slides.title: Sustainability frameworks — Brundtland to Costanza + Hickel
slides.body:
**Brundtland Report (1987)**:
- *Our Common Future* — World Commission on Environment + Development chaired by **Gro Harlem Brundtland** (Norwegian PM).
- Defined **sustainable development**: 'development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.'
- Three pillars: economic, social, environmental. Set the framing for the **1992 Rio Earth Summit** + Agenda 21 + UNFCCC + CBD + UNCCD + Rio + 10 + 20.

**UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs, 2015-2030)**:
- 17 goals + 169 targets adopted UN GA September 2015.
- Examples: SDG 1 No Poverty; SDG 2 Zero Hunger; SDG 6 Water + Sanitation; SDG 7 Affordable Clean Energy; SDG 11 Sustainable Cities; SDG 13 Climate Action; SDG 14 Life Below Water; SDG 15 Life On Land; SDG 17 Partnerships.
- 2024 mid-term review: only ~17% of targets on-track; ~85% requiring acceleration or off-track.
- Critiques: SDGs reflect compromise; growth-dependent; weak on planetary boundaries integration; inadequate equity framing.

**Planetary boundaries (Rockström 2009, 2015, 2023)**:
- **Johan Rockström** + Stockholm Resilience Centre; *Nature* 2009 'A safe operating space for humanity'.
- Nine boundaries — climate change, biosphere integrity, biogeochemical flows (N + P), land-system change, freshwater use, ocean acidification, atmospheric aerosol loading, stratospheric ozone, novel entities (chemicals + plastics).
- 2023 update (Richardson + Rockström): **6 of 9 boundaries transgressed** — climate, biosphere integrity, biogeochemical flows (N + P), land-system change, freshwater (green + blue), novel entities.
- Foundational figure for Earth-system stewardship.

**Ecological footprint — Wackernagel + Rees**:
- **Mathis Wackernagel** (with William Rees, UBC) — *Our Ecological Footprint* (1996). Measures human demand on biocapacity in global hectares per capita.
- Global footprint ~2.7 gha/person; global biocapacity ~1.6 gha/person → humanity uses ~1.7 Earths (Global Footprint Network).
- **Earth Overshoot Day** moved from late December (1971) to August 1 (2024).
- Critiques: simplifies multidimensional sustainability; misses inequality between nations; useful communication tool.

**Degrowth — Hickel et al.**:
- **Jason Hickel** — *Less is More* (2020); *The Divide* (2017). Argues high-income countries must reduce material + energy throughput to fit within planetary boundaries.
- Roots in Georgescu-Roegen, Daly, Latouche, Kallis. **Doughnut Economics (Kate Raworth 2017)** offers compatible framing — operating space between social foundation + ecological ceiling.
- Recent: degrowth incorporated into European Parliament debates 2023-2024; *Nature Sustainability* + *Nature Climate Change* papers (2022-2024) on post-growth.

**Ecosystem services — Robert Costanza**:
- **Robert Costanza** (Australian National University) — *Nature* 1997 'The value of the world's ecosystem services + natural capital' valued global ecosystem services at $33T/yr (vs. ~$25T global GDP at the time); 2014 update ~$125T/yr.
- Categories (MA 2005, IPBES): provisioning (food, fiber, water), regulating (climate, flood, pollination), cultural (recreation, spiritual), supporting (soil formation, nutrient cycling).
- Operationalized in **Payments for Ecosystem Services (PES)** schemes — Costa Rica PES (Pagos por Servicios Ambientales 1996+), New York City watershed protection (Catskills, $1.5B vs. $6-8B filtration plant), REDD + REDD+ tropical forest carbon.
- Criticisms: monetization risks; cultural + spiritual values resist pricing; commodification debates.

**Integrated frameworks (synthesis)**:
- **Doughnut Economics + Planetary Boundaries** — Raworth + Rockström merge.
- **Earth-system governance** — Biermann + Frank Earth System Governance Project.
- **Nature-based solutions (NbS)** — IUCN; ecosystem-based adaptation + mitigation; mangroves + wetlands + reforestation + agroforestry.
- **Just transition + climate justice** — IPCC AR6 WGII + WGIII recognized; central to UNFCCC negotiations.

The modern sustainability scaffolding — Brundtland → SDGs → planetary boundaries → ecological footprint → degrowth + doughnut → ecosystem services — provides the policy + analytic toolkit; geography integrates these on real places + populations.

question.question: Compute the Amazon dieback risk argument
question.goal: Estimate the cumulative + projected Brazilian Amazon deforestation in km² + assess the Nobre-Lovejoy 20-25% tipping warning.

steps.prompt: Brazilian Amazon original forest is ~4.0 M km²; ~17% lost cumulatively. How many km²?
steps.reveal: Cumulative loss ≈ 0.17 × 4.0 × 10⁶ km² ≈ **680000 km²** (INPE PRODES reports closer to 825000 km² depending on accounting boundaries; estimates vary 680000-830000 km²). For comparison, France is 643000 km² + Texas is 696000 km² — Brazil has cleared a region the size of France + change.

steps.prompt: What is the additional area to reach the Nobre-Lovejoy 20-25% threshold?

acceptedAnswers: 20-25% of 4 M km² = 800000-1000000 km²; gap ~120000-320000 km² beyond current

steps.reveal: 20% threshold = 800000 km²; 25% threshold = 1000000 km². Gap from cumulative ~680000 km² → between **+120000 km² (Iceland-sized) + +320000 km² (Italy-sized)**. At recent peak rates (~11000 km²/yr, 2021) the 20% threshold would be reached in ~11 years; at lower recent rates (~5000 km²/yr) ~25 years.

steps.prompt: What additional drivers reduce or raise the effective threshold?

acceptedAnswers: warming + drier dry season + fire + edge effects + cattle pasture lower the effective threshold; restoration + protected areas + indigenous lands raise effective resilience
warming + fire lower the threshold; protection raises it

steps.reveal: Warming (already ~1.1°C globally, more locally), drier + longer dry seasons in southern Amazon, increased fire (anthropogenic + climate-driven), forest-edge desiccation, + degraded-secondary forest mix all **lower** the effective dieback threshold. **Raising** resilience: protected areas (~25% of Brazilian Amazon), indigenous lands (~22% of Brazilian Amazon — best forest protection per Brondízio + INPE work), restoration commitments (Bonn Challenge, Initiative 20×20), supply-chain moratoria (soy + beef).

acceptedAnswers: biosphere integrity + land-system change boundaries transgressed; SDG 15 Life on Land; ecosystem services (Costanza) valuation; REDD+ payments; ecological footprint

steps.reveal: **Planetary boundaries**: biosphere integrity + land-system change boundaries already transgressed; freshwater (green-water + blue-water) under pressure. **SDGs**: 13 (Climate), 15 (Life on Land), 6 (Water), 2 (Hunger via Amazon teleconnection rainfall to Brazilian + global agriculture). **Costanza ecosystem services**: Amazon's regulating services (rainfall recycling, carbon sequestration ~150-200 Pg C, biodiversity) valued at trillions. **REDD+ + voluntary carbon** markets for forest carbon. **Hickel/degrowth**: questions the global-North commodity demand driving deforestation. **Critical**: indigenous + Quilombola governance produces best-protected forest. The Amazon case illustrates how planetary boundaries + tipping points + sustainability frameworks integrate on a real geography.

question.question: Why is the Montreal Protocol (1987) the most-cited model of successful environmental governance?
options: The **Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer (1987)** phased out CFCs + HCFCs after Molina + Rowland (1974, Nobel 1995 with Crutzen) showed CFCs destroy stratospheric ozone + Farman + British Antarctic Survey (1985 *Nature*) discovered the Antarctic ozone hole. Universal ratification (every UN state); strong compliance; Multilateral Fund (>$4B) financed developing-country transitions; iterative tightening (London 1990, Copenhagen 1992, Montreal 1997, Beijing 1999, Kigali 2016 phase-down of HFCs to avert ~0.5°C warming). Ozone hole peaked ~2000-2006; recovery expected 2060-2080 (NOAA + WMO Ozone Assessments). Lessons that made it work + are hard to replicate for climate: (1) narrow problem with measurable stratospheric link; (2) substitute chemicals existed + got cheaper; (3) industry coalition (DuPont, ICI) shifted with regulation; (4) clear + visible polar signal (the hole) + public mobilization; (5) effective bilateral diplomacy. The contrast with UNFCCC + climate negotiations reveals how harder + more diffuse climate is — emissions everywhere + decarbonization affects everything.
question.explanation: Montreal Protocol (1987) phased out CFCs after Molina+Rowland (Nobel 1995) + Farman BAS 1985 ozone hole discovery. Universal ratification, Multilateral Fund, iterative tightening (Kigali 2016 HFCs). Ozone hole recovery 2060-2080. Successful because: narrow problem, substitutes available, industry shift, visible polar signal, effective diplomacy. Hard to replicate for climate.

slides.workedSolution: Montreal Protocol (1987) — phased out CFCs + HCFCs after Molina-Rowland 1974 + Farman BAS 1985 ozone hole. Universal ratification + Multilateral Fund + iterative tightening (Kigali 2016 HFCs). Ozone recovery 2060-2080. Worked due to narrow problem, available substitutes, industry shift, visible polar signal, diplomacy. Contrast with climate exposes the difficulty of decarbonization.

question.question: A climate-adaptation strategy for Bangladesh
question.prompt: The Bangladeshi government commissions a 30-year climate-adaptation strategy. Apply the environmental + sustainability toolkit: (1) **Climate-change geography** — IPCC AR6 likely SLR 0.4-0.9 m by 2100; Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna delta projections; cyclone intensification; monsoon variability; salinization; sediment-flux changes from upstream Tibetan glaciers + Indian dams (Farakka Barrage). (2) **Vulnerable populations** — 165 M; coastal + delta exposure; livelihoods (rice, jute, shrimp, fisheries, garment factories). (3) **Planetary boundaries (Rockström)** — biodiversity (Sundarbans tigers + mangroves), freshwater (groundwater arsenic + over-extraction), land-system change. (4) **Brundtland + SDGs** — Goals 1, 6, 11, 13, 14, 15 + 17 partnerships with India + Bhutan + Nepal. (5) **Ecosystem services (Costanza)** — mangrove storm-surge protection (Mangrove for the Future); valuation of services to justify protection. (6) **Ecological footprint + degrowth (Wackernagel, Hickel)** — Bangladesh footprint <1 Earth-share; equity claims on global mitigation. (7) **Loss + damage + climate justice** — Bangladeshi diplomacy at COP27 + COP28 established loss-and-damage fund. (8) **Adaptation portfolio** — Delta Plan 2100; polder upgrades; floating + raised settlements; managed retreat; sectoral diversification; remittance economies; climate-resilient agriculture (CGIAR varieties); SEZ + garment-industry decarbonization; education + health resilience. Deliver an 8-page strategy integrating physical, social, economic, political, + ethical dimensions.

question.question: Global ecological footprint is ~2.7 gha/person + biocapacity ~1.6 gha/person. What ratio of Earths does humanity demand?
question.hint: Ratio = 2.7 / 1.6 = 1.6875 ≈ 1.7 Earths. Earth Overshoot Day (Aug 1, 2024) corresponds to this overshoot.

question.prompt: In ≤140 words, integrate environmental issues + climate-change geography + sustainability frameworks, naming at least seven figures + four frameworks.
question.rubric: Mentions: biodiversity hotspots (**Norman Myers** 1988; 36 hotspots; ~50% plants + ~43% vertebrates on 2.4% land); Amazon deforestation (INPE; Nobre-Lovejoy tipping); desertification (UNCCD); acid rain (US 1990 CAA cap-and-trade success); ozone (Molina + Rowland; **Crutzen** Nobel 1995; Farman BAS; **Montreal Protocol 1987** + Kigali 2016); plastics + 5 ocean gyres + UN INC negotiations. Climate: IPCC AR6; SLR (Bangladesh, Tuvalu); Greenland + Antarctic instability; permafrost; coral bleaching; Anthropocene (**Crutzen** 2000-2002); Great Acceleration. Sustainability frameworks: **Brundtland 1987** sustainable development; **UN SDGs 2015-2030**; **Rockström planetary boundaries 2009/2023** (6 of 9 transgressed); **Wackernagel** ecological footprint + 1.7 Earths; **Hickel** degrowth + Raworth doughnut; **Costanza** ecosystem services. Concludes: environmental geography integrates global change + frameworks on real places + populations.
